attacks.attack: Orthant-boundary tie breaking could destroy pairwise incompatibility witnesses.
attacks.evidence: Sector-sector witnesses use all nonzero horizontal coordinates (weights 3 and 1 over sqrt(13)); cap-sector witnesses use sigma/sqrt(5). They lie strictly inside the intended horizontal orthants.

attacks.attack: Changing the legal cap parameter delta could remove the witnesses.
attacks.evidence: For every 0<delta<r, h>0 while the lens intersection sphere is at x6=-ell<0, so all sector witnesses remain below the cap cut; c has x6=r>h and remains in the cap.

attacks.attack: Rotating the five horizontal Lassak cut hyperplanes could evade the K_33 obstruction.
attacks.evidence: The lens is invariant under O(5) fixing e6; rotate the explicit witness family together with the cuts, preserving all distances.

attacks.attack: A union of two sectors may avoid the far pair because one witness lies only on a shared boundary.
attacks.evidence: The constructed witnesses are strict interior points of their respective sign orthants, not boundary points.

attacks.attack: The cap-sector witness is only a closure point and could be removed by partition conventions.
attacks.evidence: The sector witness has nonzero horizontal coordinates and x6=-ell<h, so it is interior relative to all cut halfspaces; c is strictly above h. Its exact distance to c is 1.

attacks.attack: The template obstruction might accidentally assert b(6)>=33.
attacks.evidence: The theorem quantifies only over coarsenings by unions of the 33 frozen Lassak atoms. Partitions that split or redraw atoms are explicitly outside scope.

attacks.attack: The center-fixed hypercube-facet no-go may depend on a special cube orientation.
attacks.evidence: The proof starts from arbitrary Q∈O(6), chooses a maximal coordinate of z=Q^T e6, and uses a deterministic sign-balancing lemma. The same-facet squared distance 10/7 is orientation-independent.

attacks.attack: The center-fixed hypercube-facet no-go could be misused against the full R4-style transfer.
attacks.evidence: The no-go covers only untruncated Lassak lens, apex at the small-ball center, and 12 cube-facet cones. R4-style truncation, movable apex and new directions remain open escape routes.

attacks.attack: Finite or floating-point evidence could be mistaken for a universal R6 bound.
attacks.evidence: No numerical candidate is used to claim b(6)<=32. All terminal claims are exact symbolic inequalities or quantified geometric arguments.

attacks.attack: Remote unavailability of the Lassak primary PDF could be hidden.
attacks.evidence: The source manifest states the access restriction and identifies the exact secondary reconstruction source; no unread primary text is quoted or claimed as inspected.
